messages:
Nora (People Ops): Need help: my 26yo child is turning 26 next month but has a long-term disability. They live in Portugal with me (expat), have Portuguese ID and passport, and receive government disability benefits there. Can we keep them on Redwood medical and LTD after they turn 26? What proof do carriers need when the dependent is overseas?
Liam (Benefits): Good question. Carriers treat disabled dependents differently; most allow continued coverage past 26 if disability began before the age limit and the dependent is primarily supported by you. But international residency complicates things. Did the disability begin before 26?
Nora (People Ops): Yes, disabled since childhood and we claim them as dependent on US taxes (we live abroad but still file stateside). They get benefits locally but I'm primary support.
Asha (People Ops): Two quick notes: 1) For enrollment continuation we need proof of disability (SSA award letter ideally) OR equivalent medical certification from a licensed physician. 2) Many carriers insist on English translations and notarized copies for foreign docs.
Liam (Benefits): Exactly. For LTD specifically carriers often require the dependent to be on the employer medical plan first. Some carriers refuse non-US addresses; others accept with extra verification. We'll need: passport, birth certificate, physician letter (English), proof of dependency (tax return or proof of financial support), and proof of residency (utility or registration). If you can't get an SSA letter because they're abroad, a clear physician letter plus documentation of long-term disability is usually accepted initially but carrier may request more.
LegalBot: Check treaty implications for benefits if premium deductions change tax status. Also, confirm any export-controlled data restrictions before sending medical docs across borders.
Nora (People Ops): Is there a secure uploader for foreign scans? I don't want to email passports.
Liam (Benefits): Use the secure HR portal internal upload. If you need, we can generate a transient secure link. Email benefits@redwood.com with subject "QLE - foreign disabled dependent" and we'll respond with upload instructions.
BenefitsBot: Carrier turnaround is typically 7-21 business days for international cases; expect follow-up requests. We'll flag case as "international dependent" and escalate to carrier liaison.
Nora (People Ops): Thanks—I'll collect translated docs and submit. If carrier denies because of non-US address, what's fallback for LTD?
Liam (Benefits): If carrier denies LTD for non-US address, we can explore private-pay options or global-local plans; we'll connect you to global benefits partner. We'll update once carrier responds.
Nora (People Ops): Appreciate it. I'll ping once uploaded. :white_heart:
